purpose: Gemcitabine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat several types of cancer, including pancreatic cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, and bladder cancer. It is sometimes used alone and sometimes combined with other cancer medicines. Your doctor chose this medicine because it targets and slows the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow by making copies of themselves very quickly. Gemcitabine works by sneaking into cancer cells and blocking them from copying their DNA, which is like their instruction manual. Without being able to copy their DNA, the cancer cells cannot multiply and they eventually die off.
common_side_effects: You may feel very tired or weak, which is very common. You might also notice nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite. Your blood counts will likely drop, which means you could be more prone to infections, bruising, or bleeding. Flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, headache, and muscle aches can happen especially right after your treatment. Mild skin rash and swelling, particularly in your legs and feet, are also possible.
warnings: Because this medicine lowers your immune system, you are at a higher risk of getting serious infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop a fever or feel very unwell. Gemcitabine can cause serious lung problems, kidney problems, or liver problems in some patients, so your doctor will monitor you with regular blood tests. Avoid contact with people who are sick. Do not receive live vaccines during treatment. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant.
typical_dosing: Gemcitabine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter at a clinic or hospital. A typical infusion takes about 30 minutes. How often you receive it depends on your specific cancer and treatment plan, but it is commonly given once a week for several weeks followed by a rest period. Your doctor will tailor the schedule and dose specifically for you.
